recommendation: Keep the audit commit. Do not restore the extension definition to core; route future changes to the SDC IG unless core Questionnaire wording itself becomes misleading.
issue_request: FHIR-17144 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core Questionnaire issue asking how to express more complex enableWhen conditions than repeated simple enableWhen elements; the approved resolution deprecated cqif-condition and called for a 0..1 Questionnaire.item enableWhen expression extension used only when the item has no enableWhen elements.
initial_application: The Jira comment records SVN revision 13896, and imported git history includes b89387a2a19a73a179674e028fd5f93bc3826dad labelled GF#17144: Deprecate cqif-condition extension. Current core source no longer has an active cqif-condition definition and retains Questionnaire wording that points complex enableWhen logic to enableWhenExpression.
additional_context: FHIR-19527 later moved complex Questionnaire and QuestionnaireResponse extensions from core to the SDC IG and renamed questionnaire-enableWhen to questionnaire-enableWhenExpression. Current SDC source defines sdc-questionnaire-enableWhenExpression on Questionnaire.item, constrains it to Expression, documents that it is only permitted when the containing item has no enableWhen elements, and includes a behavior invariant forbidding enableWhen and enableWhenExpression together.
reconciliation: Published an empty no-change audit commit. No FHIR core source edit is needed because core remains the right place for base enableWhen behavior, while the extension definition and detailed guidance now intentionally live in SDC.
